item.name: Telegram voice/audio inbound attachment markers
item.contract: Telegram voice and audio messages produce nonblank channel-neutral submit text plus bounded attachment descriptors so downstream gateway/model paths can see media evidence instead of an empty user turn.
item.degraded_mode: If Telegram supplies media without a resolvable URL, Gormes preserves the platform file ID as redacted source evidence and still emits a readable marker rather than blank text.
ready_when: Gateway Attachment descriptors are available on InboundEvent.SubmitText.
Telegram adapter tests can inject fake voice/audio updates without live Telegram or provider calls.
not_ready_when: The implementation requires live Telegram file downloads or provider transcription calls.
Media-only updates can still become blank EventSubmit text.
acceptance: Voice-only updates emit nonblank submit text containing a Telegram voice marker and duration evidence.
Audio updates with captions preserve the caption and append a Telegram audio marker.
Attachment descriptors include kind, media type, file name where present, and source ID without fetching live media.
Slash-command parsing still runs after marker assembly and media fixtures remain hermetic.
done_signal: Telegram voice/audio fake-update tests prove media-only and captioned audio messages produce nonblank submit text and bounded attachment evidence.

provenance.note: Completes the small adapter seam that prevents Telegram voice/audio updates from entering Gormes as blank turns.

item.name: Hermes/Honcho Go runtime plan second-wave reconciliation
item.contract: A second-wave sub-agent reconciliation turns the raw Hermes/Honcho swarm findings into one canonical Go runtime implementation plan, classifying every subsystem as owned, mapped-by-symbol, mapped-by-contract, excluded, or still row-backed, with no subsystem-level unknown/gap remaining.
item.degraded_mode: If a future parity pass finds an unclassified subsystem, Gormes reports unknown_gap_in_runtime_plan and requires gormes-planner to update the runtime plan, feature map, swarm audit, upstream ledger, progress rows, and nested coverage test before builder selection.
ready_when: The source-lane swarm findings for Hermes runtime/providers, Hermes tools/security/plugins, Hermes gateway/CLI/release, Honcho core/Goncho, and Honcho SDK/MCP/CLI/deploy are available.
Second-wave reconciliation can classify large surfaces without implementing runtime code.
The pass updates only docs, planner references, tests, and progress rows.
not_ready_when: The pass tries to implement runtime code under cmd or internal.
Any subsystem remains unknown/gap without an owned, excluded, mapped, or row-backed decision.
The pass creates a side backlog outside progress.json.
unblocks: Nested feature-level coverage test matrix for swarm gaps
acceptance: Hermes/Honcho To Gormes Go Runtime Plan has the required sections: Evidence Corpus, Classification Vocabulary, Hermes Feature Map, Honcho Feature Map, Go Implementation Order, Nested Feature-Level Coverage Matrix, Swarm Gap Matrix, and Progress Register Actions.
Every broad Hermes and Honcho subsystem is classified as owned, mapped-by-symbol, mapped-by-contract, excluded, or still row-backed.
The runtime plan states that no subsystem-level unknown/gap remains after the two-wave swarm pass.
The architecture index, building index, completion plan, feature map, upstream ledger, and swarm audit link to the runtime plan.
Planner reference docs explain the full-map classification vocabulary and exact nested-ref requirement.
item.note: Complete in the 2026-04-28 gormes-planner second-wave swarm pass: source mappers fed architecture, runtime-contract, test-matrix, docs/register, and gap-classifier agents, producing a canonical Go runtime plan that maps all Hermes/Honcho subsystems without claiming implementation parity.
done_signal: The runtime plan is the canonical Hermes/Honcho-to-Gormes Go implementation map, with zero subsystem-level unknown/gap items and nested coverage protected by docs tests.

provenance.upstream_ref: two-wave swarm audit over hermes-agent current tree + honcho current tree
provenance.note: Turns full-map swarm output into an implementation-ready planning register without adding runtime code.

item.name: Session auto-reset + STT config parity
item.contract: Gormes gains Hermes-parity session reset (auto-clear sessions on inactivity/daily boundary) and STT config surface. Session reset checks the configured policy before processing each message and auto-resets stale sessions. STT config exposes enabled/provider/local model/openai model in config.toml.
item.degraded_mode: When session_reset policy is 'none', sessions persist indefinitely (legacy behavior). When STT is not configured, transcription defaults to local provider with base model.
ready_when: Config struct has STTCfg with enabled/provider/local/openai fields.
not_ready_when: Session reset policies are not implemented in manager.go.
STT config fields are missing from config.go.
acceptance: checkAutoReset() evaluates inactivity/daily/both/none policies before submitting turns.
Config struct has STTCfg with enabled/provider/local/openai fields.
done_signal: Session auto-reset works with inactivity/daily/both/none policies; STT config fields exposed in config.toml.

implementation: internal/config/config.go: STTCfg with Enabled, Provider, Local.Model, Local.Language, OpenAI.Model fields
internal/gateway/manager_test.go: TestCheckAutoReset_* covers all policy branches
evidence.tests: go test ./internal/config -count=1 | go test ./internal/gateway -run TestCheckAutoReset -count=1 | go build ./cmd/gormes

item.name: Transcribe audio tool registration + local whisper provider
item.contract: Gormes registers the existing transcribe_audio tool in the default tool registry so STT works by default with no API key. A LocalSTTProvider wraps the WASI whisper runtime (internal/wasi/whisper/) into the TranscriptionProvider interface with auto-downloading tiny.en model (~77MB from HuggingFace). Cloud STT providers (OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, XAI) are registered alongside and activate when their API keys are present.
item.degraded_mode: When the local whisper model is unavailable (first-run download failure or disk full), the transcribe_audio tool reports stt_provider_unavailable instead of crashing. Cloud providers (OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, XAI) still work if their API keys are configured.
ready_when: transcribe_audio tool exists in internal/tools/ but is unregistered.
WASI whisper runtime exists in internal/wasi/whisper/.
LocalSTTProvider wraps whisper into TranscriptionProvider interface.
registry_audio.go registers the transcription tool with local provider.
not_ready_when: The row attempts to add voice recording or voice mode — that is separate.
The row requires cloud provider API keys for basic functionality.
acceptance: LocalSTTProvider implements TranscriptionProvider with Available() and Transcribe().
transcribe_audio tool is registered via MustRegister in the default tool registry.
go build ./cmd/gormes succeeds with the non-slim build tag.
done_signal: transcribe_audio tool is registered by default; local whisper provider auto-downloads model on first use; no API key required for basic STT.

implementation: cmd/gormes/registry_audio.go:registerAudioTools registers transcribe_audio via MustRegister in default tool registry
